datasets.annotation_method: Professional translation of English MultiNLI corpus into 14 languages

data_creator_info.evidence: XNLI (Conneau et al., 2018) is a dataset for cross-lingual Natural Language Inference, which consists of professional translations of the MNLI corpus into 14 languages.

datasets.variant_notes: Version of XNLI translated to 11 Indian languages
datasets.annotation_method: Machine Translation of XNLI followed by validation by native speakers

data_creator_info.evidence: IndicXNLI (Aggarwal et al., 2022) that translates the XNLI dataset into 11 Indic languages by using Machine Translation, followed by validation by native speakers.

datasets.variant_notes: Code-mixed Hindi-English NLI from GLUECoS benchmark
datasets.annotation_method: Manual creation: Bollywood (Hindi) movie conversations as premises with manually created hypotheses in code-mixed English-Hindi

data_creator_info.evidence: GLUECoS-NLI (Khanuja et al., 2020a) is a code-mixed NLI dataset in Hindi-English, consisting of Bollywood (Hindi) movie conversations as premises, with manually created hypotheses.

datasets.source_reference: Khanuja et al., 2020a; Khanuja et al., 2020b

datasets.annotation_method: Professional translation from English PAWS dataset into six typologically diverse languages

data_creator_info.evidence: PAWS-X (Yang et al., 2019b) is a paraphrase identification dataset professionally translated from the PAWS dataset into six typologically diverse languages.

datasets.annotation_method: Translation of English COPA dataset into typologically diverse languages

data_creator_info.evidence: XCOPA (Ponti et al., 2020) is a commonsense reasoning dataset, which is a translation of the COPA dataset into 11 typologically diverse languages, including very low-resource languages such as Eastern Apurímac Quechua and Haitian Creole.

datasets.notes: MEGA evaluates on 10 of the XCOPA languages

datasets.annotation_method: Professional translation of English StoryCloze dataset into 10 typologically diverse languages

data_creator_info.evidence: XStoryCloze (Lin et al., 2022b) is created by translating the English StoryCloze dataset using professional translators into 10 typologically diverse languages.

datasets.annotation_method: Natively collected information-seeking QA by speakers of typologically diverse languages

data_creator_info.evidence: TyDiQA (Clark et al., 2020) is a QA dataset covering 11 typologically diverse languages.

datasets.notes: MEGA evaluates on 9 of the TyDiQA languages using the Gold-P subtask. Evaluation on validation data since no public test set.

datasets.annotation_method: Professional translation of extractive QA dataset into 7 languages

data_creator_info.evidence: MLQA (Lewis et al., 2020) is an extractive QA dataset translated into 7 languages by professional translators.

datasets.notes: No training data available for MLQA; MEGA uses SQuAD training data for English few-shot examples

datasets.annotation_method: Professional translation of a subset of the SQuAD dataset into 10 languages

data_creator_info.evidence: XQuAD (Artetxe et al., 2020) consists of professional translations of a subset of the SQuaD dataset into 10 languages.

datasets.notes: Only validation data available publicly; MEGA evaluates on validation set. Cross-lingual setup only (English few-shot examples).

datasets.annotation_method: Manually curated cloze-style reading comprehension from Wikipedia articles on Indic topics

data_creator_info.evidence: IndicQA (Doddapaneni et al., 2022) is a manually curated cloze-style reading comprehension dataset... context paragraphs are chosen from Wikipedia articles whose topics are closely related to Indic culture, history, etc.

datasets.notes: Part of IndicXTREME benchmark. Context paragraphs related to Indic culture, history.

datasets.variant_notes: Part of Speech Tagging from Universal Dependencies 2.5 via XTREME benchmark
datasets.annotation_method: Expert linguistic annotation of naturally-occurring text in Universal Dependencies treebanks

data_creator_info.evidence: UDPOS (Zeman et al., 2020) is a dataset for Part of Speech Tagging taken from the Universal Dependencies 2.5 from the XTREME benchmark.

datasets.source_reference: Nivre et al., 2018; Zeman et al., 2020; Hu et al., 2020
datasets.notes: MEGA benchmarks a subset of the languages available in UDPOS. Evaluated on first 1000 examples per language.

datasets.variant_notes: Also called WikiANN; used via XTREME benchmark
datasets.annotation_method: Wikipedia sentences tagged via cross-lingual annotation projection for Person, Organization, and Location entities

data_creator_info.evidence: PANX (Pan et al., 2017) or WikiANN is a Named Entity Recognition dataset consisting of Wikipedia sentences tagged with Person, Organization and Location.

datasets.notes: Evaluated on first 1000 examples per language due to large number of languages.

datasets.variant_notes: Concatenation of WinoGender and WinoBias datasets
datasets.annotation_method: Concatenation of existing English datasets (WinoGender + WinoBias); LLMs prompted to translate English sentences into 8 target languages for gender bias evaluation

data_creator_info.evidence: The WinoMT dataset (Stanovsky et al., 2019) is created by concatenating the WinoGender and WinoBias datasets. WinoMT dataset consists of 3888 English sentences with equal distribution of Male and Female genders.

datasets.source_reference: Stanovsky et al., 2019; Rudinger et al., 2018; Zhao et al., 2018
datasets.notes: English source sentences are translated to 8 target languages by the LLMs being evaluated; gender accuracy is assessed on translations.

datasets.variant_notes: English-Spanish code-mixed sentiment analysis from GLUECoS benchmark
datasets.annotation_method: Code-mixed English-Spanish tweets annotated with SentiStrength scores

data_creator_info.evidence: The EN-ES-CS Sentiment Analysis dataset (Vilares et al., 2016), part of the GLUECoS benchmark is a code-mixed dataset consisting of English-Spanish Tweets annotated with SentiStrength scores.

datasets.source_reference: Vilares et al., 2016; Khanuja et al., 2020b

datasets.annotation_method: Online comments sourced from Wikipedia with crowdsourced toxicity labels; English training with multilingual test sets

data_creator_info.evidence: The Jigsaw dataset contains online comments sourced from Wikipedia. The training data, which is in English, contains labels pertaining to the toxicity of the comment.

datasets.notes: Training data in English; test data in 6 languages for multilingual evaluation. MEGA evaluates cross-lingual and translate-test strategies.

datasets.annotation_method: Naturally occurring article-summary pairs from BBC news in multiple languages

data_creator_info.evidence: The XLSum dataset contains article-summary pairs across 44 typologically diverse languages, ranging from high to very low-resource.

datasets.notes: Evaluated on first 1000 examples per language. Natively authored content from BBC news.
